title: Grace, Election and Calling
summary: How God takes the first step in salvation: His grace, His choosing and His call, with the Calvinist and Arminian views presented fairly.
description: Salvation begins with God. This course explains the meaning of grace, what the Bible says about God's choosing (election and predestination), how the gospel call goes out to all, and how Calvinist and Arminian Christians understand these truths differently. It closes with what election means for humility, assurance, holiness and evangelism.
objectives: Define grace and distinguish common grace from saving grace
Explain the biblical teaching on election and predestination
Present the Calvinist and Arminian views fairly
Explain the general and effectual call
Apply the doctrine of election to worship, assurance and evangelism
outcomes: Explain why salvation is by grace and not by works
Summarise the main texts on election
Distinguish the general call from the effectual call
Show why election encourages, not hinders, evangelism

modules.title: Amazing Grace
modules.intro: Grace is God's undeserved favour. This week we see what grace is, how widely God shows it, and why salvation is by grace alone.

lessons.title: What is grace?
lessons.body:
Grace is God's free, undeserved kindness to people who deserve His judgement. Mercy withholds the punishment we deserve; grace gives the blessing we do not deserve.

"For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast" (Ephesians 2:8-9).

Grace is not God's reward for good people. "If by grace, then is it no more of works: otherwise grace is no more grace" (Romans 11:6). It flows from God's own heart: "I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious" (Exodus 33:19).

lessons.title: Common grace
lessons.body:
God shows kindness to all people, believers and unbelievers alike. He "maketh his sun to rise on the evil and on the good, and sendeth rain on the just and on the unjust" (Matthew 5:45). He gives "rain from heaven, and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness" (Acts 14:17).

Theologians call this **common grace**. It includes life, food, families, government that restrains evil (Romans 13:1-4), conscience (Romans 2:14-15), and human skill in science, art and medicine.

Common grace does not save, but it shows God's goodness and leads toward repentance (Romans 2:4).

lessons.title: Saving grace
lessons.body:
**Saving grace** is God's work of rescuing sinners through Christ. Because sinners are "dead in trespasses and sins" (Ephesians 2:1), they need more than advice; they need life. "God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us, even when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ" (2:4-5).

No one comes to Christ unless drawn: "No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him" (John 6:44).

Arminian Christians speak of **prevenient grace**: grace that goes before, enabling every person to respond freely. Calvinists speak of **irresistible** or effectual grace given to the elect. Both agree that without grace no one would come.

terms.def: God's free, undeserved favour to sinners.
God withholding the punishment we deserve.
God's kindness to all people that does not save, such as rain, food and conscience.
God's work through Christ that rescues sinners from sin and death.
In Arminian teaching, grace that goes before and enables every person to respond to God.
In Calvinist teaching, grace that certainly brings the elect to faith; also called irresistible grace.

If salvation is by grace, it is no more of works.

Arminians speak of prevenient grace; Calvinists of effectual grace; both say salvation begins with God.

modules.title: Chosen in Christ
modules.intro: The Bible teaches that God chooses. This week we study the key texts on election and predestination.

lessons.title: The language of choosing
lessons.body:
Election means God's choosing. God chose Israel, not because they were great, but because He loved them (Deuteronomy 7:6-8).

The New Testament speaks of believers as chosen: God "hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy" (Ephesians 1:4). Believers are "elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father" (1 Peter 1:2). Jesus said, "Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you" (John 15:16).

**Predestination** means God's deciding beforehand: He "predestinated us unto the adoption of children by Jesus Christ" (Ephesians 1:5).

lessons.title: The golden chain
lessons.body:
Romans 8:29-30 lists God's saving acts in order: "whom he did foreknow, he also did predestinate to be conformed to the image of his Son... whom he did predestinate, them he also called: and whom he called, them he also justified: and whom he justified, them he also glorified."

This is sometimes called the **golden chain of salvation**. Each link is God's work, and none is lost from first to last.

The goal of predestination is Christlikeness: "to be conformed to the image of his Son". Election is not just about who goes to heaven; it is about God making a holy family.

lessons.title: Romans 9 and God's purpose
lessons.body:
In Romans 9 Paul explains why many Israelites rejected Christ. God chose Jacob over Esau before they were born, "that the purpose of God according to election might stand, not of works, but of him that calleth" (9:11).

Paul answers objections: "Is there unrighteousness with God? God forbid" (9:14). He shows God's freedom: "So then it is not of him that willeth, nor of him that runneth, but of God that sheweth mercy" (9:16).

Yet the same section ends with human responsibility: "whosoever shall call upon the name of the Lord shall be saved" (10:13). Both truths stand together in Scripture.

modules.title: Two Views of Election
modules.intro: Christians who love the Bible understand election in two main ways. This week we present each view fairly, with its texts and concerns.

lessons.title: The Calvinist view
lessons.body:
Following Augustine and John Calvin, Reformed Christians (including Reformed Baptists) teach **unconditional election**: God chose some for salvation not because of anything foreseen in them, but purely by His grace.

They stress that sinners are spiritually dead and cannot believe unless God first gives new life (Ephesians 2:1-5). Faith itself is God's gift. "As many as were ordained to eternal life believed" (Acts 13:48).

They see foreknowledge as God setting His love on people beforehand. This view is often summarised as TULIP, from the Synod of Dort (1619).

lessons.title: The Arminian view
lessons.body:
Following Jacob Arminius and John Wesley, many Christians, including Methodists, Holiness churches such as Deeper Life, most Pentecostals and many Baptists, teach **conditional election**: God chose those whom He foreknew would believe.

They stress that God "will have all men to be saved" (1 Timothy 2:4) and is "not willing that any should perish" (2 Peter 3:9). By prevenient grace, everyone is enabled to respond.

They see election as corporate (God chose a people in Christ) and conditional on faith (1 Peter 1:2), and they emphasise genuine human responsibility to believe.

lessons.title: Holding the tension
lessons.body:
Both views seek to honour Scripture. Calvinists fear that conditional election makes salvation depend on man; Arminians fear that unconditional election makes God seem unfair and weakens human responsibility.

Both agree on essentials: salvation is by grace through faith; no one is saved by works; God is sovereign and good; people are responsible to repent and believe; the gospel must be preached to all.

Charles Spurgeon, a Calvinist Baptist, refused to choose between these truths, saying he did not need to reconcile friends. Some compare them to two railway lines that seem to meet only at the horizon. Humility, not pride, should mark how we hold our view (Romans 11:33-36).

modules.title: The Call of God
modules.intro: God calls through the gospel. This week we study the general and effectual call and how election should shape our lives.

lessons.title: The general call
lessons.body:
The gospel invitation goes out to everyone. "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden" (Matthew 11:28). "Whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely" (Revelation 22:17). God "commandeth all men every where to repent" (Acts 17:30).

This is the **general** or outward call. It is sincere: God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked (Ezekiel 33:11).

Yet not all respond. "Many are called, but few are chosen" (Matthew 22:14). People who reject the call are responsible for their choice (John 5:40).

lessons.title: The effectual call
lessons.body:
Scripture also speaks of a call that brings people to Christ. Those who are "called" in Romans 8:30 are also justified. Paul says God "called us with an holy calling" (2 Timothy 1:9), and "called you out of darkness into his marvellous light" (1 Peter 2:9).

Lydia shows how this works: "whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul" (Acts 16:14).

Calvinists call this the **effectual call**, which always succeeds. Arminians see the inward call as grace that can be accepted or resisted (Acts 7:51). Both pray for God to open hearts.

lessons.title: Living as the chosen
lessons.body:
Election is meant to shape how we live:

- **Humility**: "What hast thou that thou didst not receive?" (1 Corinthians 4:7).
- **Assurance**: our salvation rests on God's purpose, not our strength.
- **Holiness**: chosen "that we should be holy" (Ephesians 1:4); "give diligence to make your calling and election sure" (2 Peter 1:10).
- **Evangelism**: Paul endured all things "for the elect's sakes, that they may also obtain the salvation" (2 Timothy 2:10). God told Paul in Corinth, "I have much people in this city" (Acts 18:10).

We do not know who the elect are; we preach to all.

assignments.title: Election and evangelism
assignments.prompt: Some say, "If God has chosen who will be saved, why should I evangelise?" Write a reply using at least five passages from this course, showing how both Calvinist and Arminian Christians answer this question.

assignments.title: Comparing the two views
assignments.prompt: Present the Calvinist and Arminian views of election fairly. For each, give its main texts, its strongest point and the concern it raises about the other view. Close with what you have learned about holding such doctrines with humility.
